NATIONAL FOREWORD

This Indian Standard (Part 2) which is identical with ISO 7216 : 1992 'Acoustics - Agricultural and forestry wheeled tracters and self-propelled machines - Measurement of noise emitted when in motion' issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of the Agricultural Tractors and Power Tillers Sectional Committee and approval of the Food and AgriCUlture Division Council. This standard was first published in 1987 and based on ISO 5131 : 1982 and DIS 7216. With the revision of ISO 5131 in 1996 it has been decided to revise this standard also. This standard will be published in two parts. This part (Part 2) covers measurement of noise when tractor in motion and Part 1 covers method of measurement at operator's ear level. In the adopted standard certain terminology and conventions are not identical to those used in Indian Standards. Attention is drawn specially to the following: a) Wherever the words 'International Standard' appear, referring to this standard. they should be read as 'Indian Standard'. b) Comma (.) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards the current practice is to use a point (.) as the decimal marker. In this standard, the following International Standards is referred to. Read in its respective place, the following:

In reporting the resultsof a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'.

1

Scope

This International Standard specifies a method for

3.1 agricultural tractor: A self-propelled wheeled machine having at least two axles, or a lrack-lavinq machine. particularly designed to pull, push, carry
and operate implements used for agricultural work (including forestry work). It may be provided with a detachable loading platform.

rneasuring the A-weighted sound pressure level of the noise emitted by agricultural and forestry wheeled tractors and self-propelled machines. fitted with elastic tyres, the noise being measured while the vehicle is in motion.

11 IS not applicable to special forestry machinery, for example, forwarders, skldders, etc., as defined in ISO 6814.
NOTE 1 The test method calls for an acoustical environment which can only be obtained in an eXlensive open space.

3.2 agricultural self-propelled machine: A machine, other than a tractor, having its own means of propulsion and normally intended for use in agriculture and forestry.

4 Instrumentation
measuring device is a sound level meter meeting or exceeding the requirements of a type 1 instrument in accordance with lee 651.

4.2 If alternative measuring equipment including.
for example, a tape recorder and/or level recorder. is used, the tolerances of the several sections of the measuring chain shall not exceed the tolerances given in relevant clauses of lEe 651. If a tape recorder is used as part of the measuring equipment. it may be necessary to include suitable weighting networks for recording and reproduction to provide an adequate slqnal-to-noise ratio over the whole frequency range of interest.

4.3 The calibration of the equipment at the time of
measurements shall be. in all respects, in accordance with the specifications of lEe 651 for a type 1 instrument. Checking of the calibration shall be carried out at appropriate intervals and at least before and after each measurement session, using an acoustical calibrator in accordance with the specifications of lEe 942 for a class 1 instrument

lEe 942:1988. Sound CAlibrators.

5 Meteorologlc.l condition.
The test shall not be carried out In adverse weather conditions which are likely to affect the measurements.
The wind velocity measured at 1,2 m above ground level shall not exceed an average value of 5 mls Iveraged over a 30 8 period, or 8 maximum value of 8 m/s during the test period. For wind speeds In excels of 1 mi', a microphone windscreen shall be used; appropriate compensation for the effects of Its use shall be allowed for In the calibration.

Layout of the t��t are.

8.1 The centreline of the track (cc), a line (PP)
perpendicular to it and passing through the centre of the test area and two lines (AA and BS) parallel to line PP and 10 m from it shall be marked on the track (see figure 1).

8 B8ckground nol..
The A-weighted sound pressure level of the background noise, Including wind notse, shall be at least 10 dB below that produced by the machine being tested.

8.2 The microphone positions shall be located on
the line PP on each side of the centreline and 7,5 m from It as shown in figure 1. The microphone shall be 1,2 m above ground level. The microphone shall be oriented in a direction normal to the centreline of the path of travel on the track.

7

Acouatlc81 environment

7.1 The test site shall consist of a track across a
substantially level, open space. It shall be such that hemispherical divergence exists between the noise source and the microphone to within � 1 dB. This condition Is deemed to be satisfied if, within a radius of not less than 50 m, there are no objects (such as buildings, solid fences, rocks and other machines) likely to renect slgnincant sound.

9

Machine conditions

7.2 The surface of an area having a radius not less than 10 m about the centre of the site (the test area) shall consist of smooth concrete, asphalt or slmtlar hard material, dry and free from acoustically ab-

9.1 The machine being tested shall comply with the manufacturer's specincauons and shall be operated in accordance with published instructions. It shall be unladen and unballasted and, except in the case of non-separable machines, be without trailer or semi-trailer.

9.2 Immediately before the test, the engine shall
be brought to its normal operating temperatures.

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis ofcomments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is takenup for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 'BIS Handbook' and 'Standards: Monthly Additions'.
